author: AndreyPavlenko
title: GPU unit tests fail to extract OpenVINO package - tbb12.dll locked (Access denied) on Windows self-hosted runner
signature: remove item cannot remove item access to the path is denied unauthorizedaccessexception|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails with PowerShell Remove-Item access denied on tbb12.dll during Expand-Archive -Force overwrite

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
At C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive.psm1:1029
+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : RemoveFileSystemItemUnAuthorizedAccess,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.RemoveItemCommand
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force, which tries to delete pre-existing files (tbb12.dll) in the install directory before re-extracting. The file is still locked by another process (likely a lingering handle from a previous OpenVINO test/build process or Windows Defender scan on this self-hosted Windows runner) or has residual restrictive ACLs from a prior job, so PowerShell's Remove-Item raises UnauthorizedAccessException and the step exits with code 1. This is a recurring, runner-state issue rather than a code defect: the same signature has now been observed 4 times (prior to this run) in the last ~24 hours, all on Windows self-hosted runners performing the same extraction step, unrelated to the specific PR content.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires the exact state of a Windows self-hosted runner (stale file lock/ACL on tbb12.dll in the shared install directory) that cannot be reliably reproduced locally. Can be approximated locally on Windows by holding tbb12.dll open (e.g., loading the DLL into a running process) and then invoking 'Expand-Archive -Force' against an archive containing the same file path.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'GPU unit tests' job (or the whole run) - this is a transient runner-state issue and a clean runner slot/VM typically succeeds.

Have the runner cleanup/reset step forcibly terminate any lingering processes holding handles in the install directory before Expand-Archive runs (e.g., a pre-step using handle.exe/Get-Process to detect and kill lockers).
Consider extracting into a fresh unique directory per run instead of overwriting a shared install path with -Force, avoiding the delete-then-recreate race entirely.
If recurrence continues, flag the runner pool (aks-win based or dedicated GPU Windows runners) for host-level investigation (AV scanning, orphaned processes) by infra/CI maintainers.
prevention_strategies: Avoid relying on Expand-Archive -Force against a long-lived shared install directory on Windows runners; prefer extracting to a clean temp directory and atomically swapping/moving it into place. Add a pre-extraction step that verifies no process holds a handle to files under the install directory (or simply deletes and recreates the directory outside of Expand-Archive's own overwrite logic, with retries/backoff for transient locks).
historical_context: This is the 5th occurrence of this exact signature (95bb23aa2ed8a84d) recorded in the CI Doctor MQ database, with the first occurrence at 2026-11-09T19:06:46Z and 3 of the prior 4 occurrences falling within the last 12 hours - previously affecting PR #39034 and #39444, none of which were related in code content to this PR (#39668, GPU/MLIR MSVC compilation fix). This confirms the failure is infrastructure-related and not tied to specific PR changes.
